title: Opsorama scene definition
description: A scene file for @opsorama/core: { schemaVersion: 1, nodes: [...] }. The schema checks structure, types and ranges; validateScene from @opsorama/core also checks unique IDs, parents, attachments and asset options, and reports each problem with a fix.

schemaVersion.description: Format version; 1 is the only version.

nodes.description: Every node of the scene. IDs must be unique.

SceneDefinition.description: A scene file: visual nodes only. Settings, camera and host data are not part of it. Check one with `validateScene`, or against the published JSON Schema `@opsorama/core/scene-definition.schema.json`.

SceneNode.description: One visual node of a scene; `kind` selects its fields.

id.description: Unique node ID within the scene. Used for updates, selection and references from `parentId` and `attachment.nodeId`.

parentId.description: Containing asset or group: the node uses its local coordinates and shows only while that asset's `view` is not `'closed'` (a group always shows its children). Any asset or group can be a parent; missing parents remain dormant. Exclusive with `attachment`. See `validateParents`.

attachment.description: Carries the node on another node, at its origin or a named anchor; the transform becomes local to it. Exclusive with `parentId`.

entityId.description: ID of the host record this node represents. A node with an `entityId` is selectable, and selections report it.

label.description: Projected HTML label text, escaped safely.

labelMode.description: `always` (default) shows the label at all times; `active` only while the node is hovered or selected.

position.description: Metres in world space, or in the container's local space with `parentId`. Default [0, 0, 0].

scale.description: Per-axis scale factors. Default [1, 1, 1]. Never encode quantities with scale; use `count`.

selectable.description: `true` makes the node selectable without an `entityId`; `false` keeps a node with an `entityId` out of selection by click or label, for example a floor area whose records are shown elsewhere. The host can still select it with `store.select`. Default: selectable when it has an `entityId`.

size.description: Width (x) and depth (z) in metres, both greater than 0.

color.description: Surface color, a CSS color. Default #e7eef8.

interior.description: Declares this node's footprint an indoor area: nodes whose pivot lies inside it, and the area itself, neither cast nor receive shadows. Default false. See `interiorAreas`.

GroundNode.description: A shadow-receiving platform under the scene.

anchor.description: Named anchor of the carrier's model, such as a carry or fork anchor. Default: the carrier's origin.

Attachment.description: A child owns its resources and identity; its transform is local to the parent's named anchor.

Vec3.description: `[x, y, z]`: metres for positions (Y is up), radians for Euler rotations, factors for scale.

VisualState.description: Optional host visual alert. Model-native support is opt-in; neutral geometry ignores it.

asset.description: Name of a model in the renderer's asset registry.

interior.description: Sized surface assets with an explicit `footprint` only: declares that footprint an indoor area, like `GroundNode.interior`. Default false.

localMotion.description: Disable built-in model animation only; scene/reduced-motion gates always win.

materials.description: Per-instance semantic colors for models that declare palette support, keyed by material role.

view.description: Container view for the nodes whose `parentId` names this asset: `'closed'` (default) hides them, `'peek'` and `'open'` show them. Models may change their look with it (the building lowers its walls). Set it with `setNodeView`.

peekOnHover.description: Opt-in mouse preview: hovering the model's container bounds (`userData.containerBounds` set by its factory) peeks it after 160 ms and closes the peek after 280 ms outside. Hosts must still provide an explicit open/close control. Default false.

options.description: Model-specific options as plain JSON-like data, validated by the asset's factory; see `AssetOptions`. A change rebuilds the model.

color.description: Optional material color override, a CSS color, for factories that support it.

variant.description: Factory-specific variant name; the model's descriptor lists its variants.

count.description: Visible quantity for countable models, within the model's declared range or variants. Default: the model's default.

multiplier.description: Disclosed symbolic factor: the represented total is count × multiplier. Adds no geometry. Default 1.

countLayout.description: `compact` or `reserved` (keep maximum-capacity slots) for models that support count layouts.

footprint.description: Sized surface assets only (floor, terrain, sidewalk): width × depth in metres.

AssetNode.description: A model from the renderer's asset registry, such as a catalog object from `@opsorama/objects`.

speed.description: Default travel speed in metres per visual second, greater than 0 and at most 30.

items.description: Metres per visual second, greater than 0 and at most 30 (`MAX_ROUTE_SPEED`).

segmentSpeeds.description: Optional per-segment speeds (length `points.length - 1`), e.g. lane speed limits.

stops.description: Timed pauses at route points, in any order; one per point.

loop.description: Restart from the first point after the last; requires a closed route (last point equals first).

endYaw.description: Heading in radians (rotation about Y, 0 faces +z) after a non-looping route ends.

reverseSegments.description: How many segments from the start are driven in reverse: the agent keeps its heading and backs along them, then stops before it drives forward. Default 0. Not for loops. A follower that joins this route mid-travel drives it forward.

profile.description: Kinematics of the agent kind; see `MotionProfile`.

startYaw.description: Heading before the route starts; with `profile.turnRate` the agent first turns in place. Ignored by loops.

startSpeed.description: Speed at the first point in m/s (0–30), e.g. when a replacement joins mid-travel. Default 0. Used with `profile.acceleration`; ignored by loops.

elapsed.description: Seconds of this route already travelled when a follower first takes it, so a newly mounted renderer resumes mid-route instead of restarting (loops wrap; at or beyond the end a one-way route is finished). Not part of the route's identity: a follower that already follows the route keeps its own progress. Default 0. `behaviorNode(state, base, { time })` sets it from simulation time.

index.description: Index into `points` where the follower pauses; at most one stop per point.

seconds.description: Visual seconds to remain at the point, greater than 0 and at most 3600.

yaw.description: Optional heading while stopped, e.g. facing a shelf or desk.

RouteStop.description: A visual route assigned to an asset node. The follower owns the node's root position and heading while the route is present; `position` stays the host's record position and is used again after the route is removed.

acceleration.description: Acceleration and braking in m/s² (greater than 0, at most 50). Agents start, stop and change lane speed smoothly.

turnRate.description: Turning rate in rad/s (greater than 0, at most 50) while standing: at the start, at stops, at the end and at sharp corners.

turnInPlaceAngle.description: Corners sharper than this angle (radians, 0–π) are not taken while moving: the agent brakes to a stop (with `acceleration`) and turns in place (with `turnRate`). Default π/4 when `turnRate` is set; otherwise π, which never stops.

cornerSpeed.description: Speed through a 90° corner taken while moving, in m/s; requires `acceleration`. Shallower corners interpolate toward full speed, sharper ones use this value. Greater than 0, at most 30.

cornerRadius.description: Radius in metres (greater than 0, at most 50) of corners taken while moving: the agent drives a circular arc tangent to both segments instead of pivoting on the corner point. Short segments shrink the arc so it never uses more than half of either one. Timing stays on the polyline, so `routeDuration`, `routeTimes` and arrival times do not change: the arc is covered in the time of the two corner legs it replaces, a little slower than the reported speed. Corners where the agent stops and turns in place stay sharp.

MotionProfile.description: How an agent kind moves along a route. Every field is optional; without a profile, speed changes and turns are instant (the renderer only blends the heading). The profile is part of the route, so simulation time (`routeDuration`) and visual time stay identical.

kind.description: Name of a controller factory in the renderer's registry.

options.description: Options passed to the factory: plain JSON data with finite numbers.

NodeController.description: A per-frame motion controller assigned to an asset, shape or group node by name. The scene definition stays serializable; the renderer resolves `kind` in its controller registry (`basicControllers` plus the host's own).

ControllerValue.description: JSON data accepted in controller options, so scene definitions stay serializable.

NodeTransfer.description: Animation of a node that changes `attachment` or `parentId`, e.g. a parcel handed from a shelf to a picker. The new placement is authoritative at once; the renderer moves the node from its previous world pose to the new one over `seconds` of the visual clock (speed and pause apply), lifting it up to `arc` metres midway. Motion-off and reduced motion skip the animation. A node that first appears, or keeps its parent, does not animate.

MaterialOverrides.description: #RRGGBB colors for some material roles; omitted roles keep their defaults.

NodeView.description: Container view of an asset; see `AssetNode.view`. Default `'closed'`.

AssetOptions.description: Model-specific options of an asset node, keyed by option name. Core only requires plain JSON-like data (objects, arrays, strings, finite numbers, booleans and null) and deep-freezes it in the store; which asset accepts which option, and the option's value rules, belong to the asset's factory (`AssetFactory.validate` in `@opsorama/three`). A model package declares its typed options by augmenting this interface (`declare module '@opsorama/core' { interface AssetOptions { ... } }`), as `@opsorama/objects` does for its catalog. Custom assets may use any keys.

CountLayout.description: Reserved layouts keep each part in its maximum-capacity slot as count changes.

Footprint.description: Width along local x and depth along local z, in metres. Patterns keep their real size; geometric scale would stretch them.

PathNode.description: A low-profile visual route with a dashed center line.

tone.description: Default from `state`: critical → critical, warning → warning, inactive → neutral, otherwise info.

icon.description: Default by tone: alert for critical and warning, check for success, info otherwise.

color.description: CSS colour replacing the tone's fill. The icon and rim stay white, so choose a colour that keeps contrast.

markerSize.description: Default `medium` (32 px wide). Named apart from a zone's `size` in metres.

eyebrow.description: Small caps line above the title in the card, such as a severity. 1–40 characters.

detail.description: Line under the title in the card, such as a reading. 1–160 characters.

pulse.description: Pulse a ring around the shape to draw attention. Default true for critical, false otherwise. It never runs while scene motion is off, the scene is paused or the user prefers reduced motion.

shape.description: The geometry: `{ type: 'box', size }`, `{ type: 'sphere', radius }` or `{ type: 'cylinder', radiusTop, radiusBottom, height }`.

color.description: Surface color, a CSS color. Default: the palette color described on `ShapeNode`.

opacity.description: Opacity from 0 (invisible, still pickable) to 1 (opaque, default).

ShapeNode.description: A box, sphere or cylinder with a plain material, for charts, markers of your own and simple models. The shape stands on its origin (its bottom centre is `position`), so a bar of height h at y = 0 rises from the ground. Equal geometry types and proportions share one unit geometry scaled per node, so many shapes draw as one instanced batch. Without `color` the shape shows the scene palette: its `state` color for `busy`, `warning`, `critical` and `inactive`, the `accent` role otherwise. `opacity` below 1 makes it transparent: it casts no shadow and is never instanced.

ShapeGeometry.description: Geometry of a shape node; `type` selects its fields.

size.description: Width (x), height (y) and depth (z) in metres, each greater than 0.

BoxShape.description: A box standing on the node origin: `size` is width (x), height (y) and depth (z) in metres.

SphereShape.description: A sphere resting on the node origin: its centre is `radius` above it.

radiusTop.description: Radius of the top face in metres, 0 or more.

radiusBottom.description: Radius of the bottom face in metres, 0 or more.

CylinderShape.description: A cylinder, cone or frustum standing on the node origin along +y. One radius may be 0 (a cone), not both.

width.description: Tube diameter in metres from 0 to 5; 0 (default) draws a 1-pixel line.

dashed.description: Draw dashes instead of a continuous line. Default false.

LineNode.description: A polyline through `points` in the node's local coordinates (`position`, `rotation` and `scale` apply; with `parentId`, the container's). With `width` greater than 0 it is a solid tube of that diameter, lit like a shape, and pointer events and selection hit it; with `width` 0 (default) it is a 1-pixel line that the pointer passes through. Without `color` it uses the palette's `structure` role. Its label sits 0.3 m above its origin.

GroupNode.description: A container without geometry: its children (nodes whose `parentId` names it) use its local coordinates, so moving, turning or scaling the group moves them together. A group is always open: its children show while the group shows. Selection bubbles through groups: a click on a node that is not selectable selects its nearest selectable group ancestor. A group does not make its children indoor (shadows); only asset containers do. Its label sits at its origin.

text.description: The text, 1 to 500 characters with at least one visible character; `\n` breaks lines.

size.description: Height of capital letters in metres, from 0.05 to 20. Default 0.4. Lines are 1.75 times this apart.

color.description: Text color, a CSS color. Default: the palette `text` role, else the theme's text color.

billboard.description: Face the camera from every direction (a sprite) instead of lying in the node's local x-y plane. A billboard keeps its size in metres and ignores `rotation`. Default false.

align.description: Where the node origin sits along the text and how lines align: `left`, `center` (default) or `right`.

TextNode.description: Text drawn in the scene: a flat panel in the node's local coordinates, or with `billboard` a sprite that always faces the camera. The renderer draws it with the system font stack (the font of the projected labels) into a texture, so it scales with the scene; it is not extruded geometry. The bottom of the text block sits on the node origin, and `align` decides whether the origin is at its left end, centre or right end. A flat text faces +z and reads mirrored from behind. Line breaks (`\n`) start new lines; there is no automatic wrapping. Without `color` it uses the palette `text` role, else the theme's text color. Text is transparent: it casts and receives no shadow, is not covered by the glow selection style and is never instanced. Pointer events and selection hit its whole rectangle. Canvas text is not accessible text: put information that users must read in `label`, `entityId` details or host HTML as well. Text nodes have no route or controller; put them in a group to move them. Its label sits 0.3 m above the text.

TextAlign.description: Horizontal alignment of a text node; see `TextNode.align`.

src.description: The image URL: relative, `http:`, `https:`, `blob:` or `data:image/…`, at most 1,000,000 characters. See `IMAGE_SRC_PATTERN` for the exact rule. Prefer raster images (PNG, JPEG, WebP); an SVG needs `width` and `height` attributes to load in every browser.

items.description: Metres, greater than 0 and at most 100.
items.title: width

items.title: height

size.description: Width and height in metres, each greater than 0 and at most 100.

billboard.description: Face the camera from every direction (a sprite) instead of lying in the node's local x-y plane. A billboard keeps its size in metres and ignores `rotation`. Default false.

anisotropy.description: Anisotropic filtering of the picture, an integer from 1 to 16: how many texture samples a pixel may take along a slant. Raise it, for example to 8, for an image on a plane the camera sees at a slant, such as a sign on a wall, which otherwise blurs. Higher values cost a little more graphics work for the pixels the image covers and no memory; the renderer caps them at what the graphics card supports. Default 1, plain mipmapped filtering.

ImageNode.description: A picture in the scene: a flat rectangle of `size` in the node's local coordinates, or with `billboard` a sprite that always faces the camera. The bottom edge's centre sits on the node origin, and the image is stretched to `size`, so give `size` the image's aspect ratio. The renderer loads `src` in the background and shows a neutral placeholder until it arrives; a failed load keeps the placeholder and reports an error naming the node and the URL to `onError`. Images load with `crossOrigin = 'anonymous'`, so an image from another origin needs a server that sends `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`; same-origin, `data:` and `blob:` URLs need nothing. Equal `src` values share one texture. Images are transparent where the picture is: they cast and receive no shadow, are not covered by the glow selection style and are never instanced. Pointer events and selection hit the whole rectangle. An image is not accessible content: describe essential information in `label` or host HTML. Image nodes have no route or controller; put them in a group to move them. Its label sits 0.3 m above the image.
